rv.q: The vigorous and absurd fight scenes are splendidly risky and – on a darker note – there’s real torment for Vincent Moisy’s Malvolio as darkness falls in the second half.
By the end of the night, you can … As the evening marches towards the three-hour mark… the surfeit of songs slows the action.
This is a heartening evening out, where the atmosphere is almost pantomime-like and the complicity between players and audience becomes total.
This Twelfth Night is therefore an event that feels particularly well suited to a summer evening, with the sun gradually setting as the story unfolds.
The play is fun, enjoyable, and knows when to keep to the text, and when to stray away from it.
Although it does take a little while to warm up, once it finds the balance between comedy and drama there is a lot of fun to be had with this production.
Sadly, most of it falls very flat.
Overall, it was a thoroughly enjoyable evening.
For a night of laughs under the stars after a day exploring a London landmark, there are few better options than Theatre on Kew ’s Twelfth Night .
Overall, Twelfth Night at Kew really does live up to its promise to be a fun, hilarious show.
It’s an extremely fun production and I had a lovely day out followed by theatre.
It is a delight to watch, under the stars, where magic blends with mayhem.

cn.t: Critics praise these outdoor productions for their energetic, accessible approach to Shakespeare's comedy, with inventive staging and strong audience engagement. One dissenting voice finds the execution disappointing after a promising start.
